designIntent.product: A marketing homepage for Axiom, an AI agent platform that researches, analyzes, and executes multi-step work.
designIntent.audience: High-performance individual contributors and startup teams.
designIntent.coreTask: Let a qualified visitor immediately try a deterministic product preview and understand the path from objective to outcome.
designIntent.visualDirection: Softly rounded, cinematic graphite interface with warm-white typography, one electric-cyan signal color, and selective glass depth around navigation, product previews, and conversion surfaces; no generic purple glow, indiscriminate glass-card collage, or decorative bento grid.
principles: The working product preview leads the first viewport.
Every accent color and motion cue communicates state.
Control, panel, and shell radii form a visible hierarchy instead of repeating one hard rectangle.
Glass is reserved for meaningful elevated layers and always has an opaque fallback.
Research, analysis, and execution read as one connected workflow.
Mobile preserves the desktop narrative in a single semantic order.
Keyboard access, visible focus, reflow, contrast, and reduced motion are release requirements.

dependencies.name: react
dependencies.reason: Typed component architecture and deterministic interactive demo state.

dependencies.name: tailwindcss
dependencies.reason: Design tokens, responsive composition, and reduced-motion styling.

dependencies.name: lucide-react
dependencies.reason: Recognizable action and status icons that reinforce text labels.

dependencies.name: motion
dependencies.reason: Purposeful gesture feedback, connected stage transitions, scroll-linked progress, and user-preference-aware reduced motion without introducing a second visual system.

regions.need: Navigate the marketing story and reach the primary trial action on desktop or mobile.
regions.reason: The current official shadcn/ui catalog verifies Button and Sheet, and Sheet supplies the dialog semantics required by mobile navigation.
regions.responsive: Inline links remain visible at desktop widths; at narrow widths they move into a right-side Sheet while the primary brand and menu trigger stay visible.

accessibility.keyboard: All links and controls follow document tab order; Escape closes the mobile sheet.
accessibility.focus: The menu trigger has a visible focus ring and focus returns to it after close.
accessibility.semantics: A nav landmark contains real anchor links; the menu trigger has an accessible name and the sheet has a title.

regions.need: Enter or select an objective and start the immediate product preview.
regions.reason: The current official shadcn/ui catalog verifies these form and label primitives; local composition preserves native textarea and button behavior while applying the approved control, panel, and shell radius hierarchy inside one glass product surface.
regions.responsive: The composer fills its column on desktop and spans the mobile viewport with 44-pixel-minimum controls and wrapping sample-task choices.

accessibility.keyboard: Sample tasks and run action are native buttons; the textarea remains directly editable.
accessibility.focus: The primary page CTA moves visible focus to the textarea; disabled and running actions retain perceivable focus styling.
accessibility.semantics: The textarea has a persistent label and description, while run status is not encoded in placeholder text.

regions.need: Understand the agent's current stage, evidence, and finished output while a demo runs.
regions.reason: A local typed state visualization owns no state and renders the page controller's AgentRunState; it exposes a textual step list, connected progress tracer, polite live status, source count, and expanding result summary. Tests cover all states, keyboard restart, reduced motion, and narrow reflow.
regions.responsive: A two-track console becomes a vertical ordered step list; decorative telemetry is reduced before any status text is hidden.

accessibility.keyboard: Restart is a native button and no status item is focusable unless it performs an action.
accessibility.focus: The restart action uses the shared visible focus treatment.
accessibility.semantics: An ordered list expresses progression and a polite live region announces only meaningful state transitions.

regions.customReason: The signature connected agent-execution timeline is the product-specific hero evidence and no selected foundation primitive expresses its domain states as one visualization.
rejectedCandidates: shadcn/ui Progress — verifies scalar completion but cannot communicate the named Research, Analyze, and Execute stages with their evidence and outputs.

regions.need: Explain how research, analysis, and execution combine into one workflow.
regions.reason: A semantic ordered section uses shared tokens and icon-label pairs; a viewport-triggered line draw reveals the three stages as one connected process while preserving a fully visible reduced-motion state.
regions.responsive: The horizontal sequence becomes a vertical ordered narrative with the same content and DOM order.

accessibility.keyboard: The explanatory region adds no unnecessary tab stops.
accessibility.focus: Any embedded anchor uses the global visible focus treatment.
accessibility.semantics: A heading and ordered list communicate sequence independently of connectors or color.

regions.customReason: This is marketing composition rather than a behavioral primitive; local semantic markup avoids importing a second visual system.
rejectedCandidates: shadcn/ui Card — repeated isolated cards would weaken the required connected workflow narrative.

regions.need: Inspect a believable objective, execution plan, sources, and deliverables in one product surface.
regions.reason: A read-only local composition renders typed demo data into plan and output regions; one translucent outer workspace establishes product depth while quieter inner panels avoid nested-glass overload. Tests cover loading, empty, error, and success presentations plus mobile reading order.
regions.responsive: Side-by-side plan and output panels stack with objective and plan before deliverables; dense metadata wraps without horizontal page overflow.

accessibility.keyboard: The read-only surface introduces no tab stops except real artifact links.
accessibility.focus: Artifact links share the global focus ring and maintain a visible target at zoom.
accessibility.semantics: Named sections, ordered plan steps, textual status, and source labels preserve meaning without the visual grid.

regions.customReason: The workspace is a product-specific composite view, while generic cards or tables would fragment its objective-to-output narrative.
rejectedCandidates: shadcn/ui Card — useful as a primitive but insufficient as the product-specific plan and artifact workspace composition.
shadcn/ui Table — unnecessary for the small ordered dataset and less usable on narrow screens.

regions.need: Connect platform claims to useful outcomes and tool categories without fabricating customers or partnerships.
regions.reason: The current official shadcn/ui catalog verifies Badge, Separator, and Button. Each scenario is mapped to a deterministic demo task so its native button can load and start the corresponding workflow in the existing composer.
regions.responsive: Evidence labels wrap, scenarios stack, and the integration strip becomes a multi-row list with no horizontal marquee dependency.

accessibility.keyboard: Each use-case action is a native button that activates with Enter or Space; static proof points add no tab stops.
accessibility.focus: Use-case buttons and links use the global visible focus treatment.
accessibility.semantics: Section headings and lists provide grouping; every use-case button names the workflow it starts, and icon marks are decorative when adjacent text names the category.

regions.need: Return an informed visitor to the immediate trial path.
regions.reason: The verified foundation Button supplies consistent action states; a rounded translucent conversion surface visually returns to the hero material, and the action scrolls to and focuses the existing composer rather than inventing a second form.
regions.responsive: The CTA remains full-width only on small screens and does not become a sticky obstruction.

accessibility.keyboard: The native button activates with Enter or Space and moves focus predictably.
accessibility.focus: A high-contrast ring remains visible against the dark final section.
accessibility.semantics: The action label states the result: Start with a task.
